nodes.title: End-to-end packet work surfaced five wire-format bugs: exposed nonce, divergent sig scope CCSDS vs SNLP, missing ingest bounds check, inconsistent SNLP header size, accidental frame alignment
nodes.description:
Running real packets through the gateway revealed the wire format had drifted in five distinct ways. Each bug was small in isolation but together they made the wire non-portable across tiers.

Sources:
- 054d006 (VOID-110/111/112/113/114B landmark PR): names all five — nonce reuse risk, sig scope 'different for CCSDS vs SNLP', ingest handler missing length check, SNLP header size not locked, packet sizes accidentally aligned.

nodes.title: Fix all five wire invariants in a single landmark PR (not piecemeal)
nodes.description: Audit landing plan: bundle nonce + sig scope + bounds + header + alignment fixes into one reviewable change so the wire state after landing is internally consistent — rather than five partial PRs that each leave the wire in a half-changed state.

nodes.title: Piecemeal fixes — one PR per bug
Landmark PR covering all five invariants (VOID-110/111/112/113/114B)
VOID-110/111/112/113/114B landed: deterministic nonce, offsetof sig scope, length-before-cast, SNLP header locked to 14B, VOID-114B per-field + frame alignment via _tail_pad
nodes.description:
Landmark audit-driven PR.

Sources:
- 054d006 / fd3a4fa (PR #1): 'Remove 4-byte wire nonce from Packet B. ChaCha20 nonce is now derived deterministically as sat_id[4] || epoch_ts[8]... Makes nonce reuse physically impossible. Signature scope is now identical across CCSDS and SNLP... uses offsetof(PacketB_t, signature). SNLP header locked at 14 bytes — 14 is the only size that maintains 6 (mod 8) congruence with the CCSDS header. VOID-114B: Per-field natural alignment for Packets A, B, L under both tiers, plus frame-total 8-byte alignment.'
- 6c87b8a: 'VOID-114B: enforce 32/64-bit packet alignment via static_asserts'

nodes.title: Wire format unified across tiers: all packet frames % 8 == 0, sig scope 106 body bytes both tiers, nonce undiscoverable on the wire, SNLP = 14B header locked
nodes.description: Post-landmark state: 8 packet types × 2 tiers all satisfy % 4 == 0, % 8 == 0, ≤ 255 byte LoRa ceiling. Sig scope binds via offsetof — auto-adapts to any future body reshape. SNLP and CCSDS bodies are identical under their respective headers.

nodes.title: Go and C++ can still silently drift apart — nothing binds the two implementations byte-for-byte
nodes.description: The wire-format invariants are now correct in each implementation in isolation, but there's no cross-implementation ground truth. A future refactor in Go could drift from C++ without any test catching it.

nodes.title: Lock wire format against silent drift via checked-in golden vectors + cross-impl regression + CI gate
nodes.description: Two choices: (a) runtime assertions that only catch what you assert, (b) byte-reproducible vectors checked into the repo that both Go and C++ test against. Chose (b) — makes drift impossible to land.

nodes.title: VOID-123/124/125/126 landed: 14 checked-in golden .bin vectors (7 packets × 2 tiers), Go regression suite, C++ GoogleTest suite (sign+verify byte-reproducible), CI gate runs all three + vector regen-diff
nodes.description:
Cross-impl ground truth established.

Sources:
- 26ef17d / 315c294 (PR #2): 'Extend generate_packets.go with --deterministic and --out flags that emit 14 byte-reproducible .bin vectors... checked in as the single source of truth that the Go (VOID-124) and C++ (VOID-125) regression suites will cross-validate against, preventing silent wire-format drift.'
- a5c2613 / 585a53c (PR #3): 'test_sign_verify.cpp — rebuilds Packet B in C++ from the VOID-123 deterministic inputs, signs via libsodium Ed25519... asserts byte-for-byte equality with the committed packet_b.bin. Strongest possible cross-impl guarantee.' Plus vectors-drift CI job regenerates and diffs against checked-in bins.

nodes.title: Cross-impl wire drift impossible to merge: any PR that shifts a byte fails CI. PacketB byte-for-byte reproducible from deterministic inputs across Go + C++.
PacketD (0xD0) and PacketAck-SNLP (0xAC) both have 122-byte bodies — a single RF bit-flip on an adjacent field could misroute the gateway's dispatch

nodes.title: VOID-006 F-03 + C-02: magic byte discriminant (Hamming-4) absorbed from head pad, application-layer CCSDS version gate
nodes.description:
F-03 solution: 1-byte magic absorbed from existing head pad — no size change. Hamming distance 4 between 0xD0 and 0xAC guarantees a single bit-flip cannot cross types. Enforced at KSY (dispatch_122 routes on peeked magic), C++ (offsetof static_asserts), and gateway (app-layer magic check before Kaitai dispatch).

C-02: Kaitai 'valid:' unsupported on computed instance fields — CCSDS version enforcement moved to gateway app layer.

Sources:
- 5aaf137 / 5627f0e (PR #4): F-03 three-layer enforcement
